title: Government Promises Rent Subsidies as Cali Mayor Pegs Reconstruction at $3.2 Billion Over Three Years
detail: A week after the magnitude-7.4 earthquake, Colombia's government promised rent subsidies and temporary housing support for families left homeless, alongside plans to formalize an economic emergency decree. In hard-hit Cali, 46 buildings had collapsed and 533 more were ordered evacuated, with rescue operations continuing at seven sites. Cali Mayor Alejandro Eder estimated the city's reconstruction alone would cost approximately $3.2 billion over three years, with roughly 40% earmarked for humanitarian assistance and the remainder for infrastructure repair and seismic retrofitting. Nationally, the quake had killed at least 287 people, left 194 missing, destroyed about 26,000 homes, and damaged 127,000 more.

media.caption: Displaced families await rent subsidies a week after Colombia's earthquake

title: Shakira and Howard Buffett Pledge $1.25 Million to Rebuild Ten Chocó Schools
detail: Colombian singer Shakira made a surprise visit to Quibdó, the capital of earthquake-hit Chocó, alongside Howard Graham Buffett — son of investor Warren Buffett — and representatives of CAF (Development Bank of Latin America) and her Barefoot Foundation. Shakira announced a $1.25 million contribution from herself, Global Citizen, Live Nation, and CAF to rebuild schools damaged by the quake, including a pledge to rebuild the Universidad Tecnológica del Chocó, and said she would partner with Buffett to build ten new schools in Quibdó and rural Chocó. The Howard G. Buffett Foundation committed separate funding to rebuild ten additional schools in the department, one of Colombia's poorest and hardest-hit by the disaster.

media.caption: Shakira and Howard Buffett tour earthquake-damaged Quibdó and pledge school reconstruction funds
